title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 predictions: Expert picks for matches in Saudi Arabia - CBS Sports
description: Raw and SmackDown's world champions collide for the Crown Jewel championships
body:
Raw and SmackDown's world champions collide for the Crown Jewel championships
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        World champions collide at WWE Crown Jewel, but there's more than a ceremonial title at stake for Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. They are set to unearth years of Bloodline baggage in Saturday's main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.Reigns and Zayn, Raw and SmackDown's respective world champions, were in a very different place nearly four years ago. In February 2023, Zayn, the underdog fighting in his backyard, nearly dethroned Reigns for the undisputed WWE world heavyweight championship. He fell short of that career-defining moment. Zayn eventually won two world titles and can tie up one more loose end by finally beating Reigns.That's not the only Crown Jewel championship set for this weekend. Women's world champion Liv Morgan and WWE women's champion Chelsea Green clash for the women's crown. Similar to Zayn, Green had never won a world title before this year. She shocked the world by winning the interim WWE women's title in a ladder match before graduating to full-time champion. Morgan is one win away from becoming the only person, man or woman, to win a Crown Jewel title twice.There are only two other matches scheduled to take place on Saturday. Most notably, it's expected to be the end of the long-running feud between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton. The two have been going at it off and on since WrestleMania season in April after Orton delivered a vicious punt to Rhodes at the conclusion of the match. Now, the two look to settle their differences in a Last Man Standing match. 

        
            
                WWE Crown Jewel 2026 card: Complete list of matches and participants set for Saudi Arabia
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Plus, The Vision -- Bron Breakker and Austin Theory -- make their first defense of the tag team titles when they take on Penta and Je'Von Evans. Of note, Penta currently holds the Money in the Bank briefcase and could be an interesting angle to the main event later in the night.With so much action set for Saturday, the CBS Sports wrestling experts sat down to make their picks for who will emerge victorious at Crown Jewel.WWE Crown Jewel Championship -- World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns vs. Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn: Run 100 simulations and Zayn beats Reigns once. This is the one. There was genuine fan appetite for Zayn, who'd reached new heights after splitting from The Bloodline, to dethrone Reigns at Elimination Chamber in 2023. Invigorated by his hometown crowd in Montreal, Zayn nearly delivered. But WWE was never pivoting from having Rhodes beat Reigns at WrestleMania two months later. Zayn will avenge that loss this weekend, receiving a hero's welcome in Riyadh, albeit a more muted version of the one he got in Montreal. Reigns' world heavyweight title isn't on the line, so he can afford to lose. It won't come without a lot of interference from The 946, who are actively feuding with The Bloodline and seem on track for a WarGames match with Reigns' family, but Zayn will get it done.  Pick: Sami Zayn wins -- Shakiel Mahjouri (also Brent Brookhouse)
WWE Women's Crown Jewel Championship -- Women's World Champion Liv Morgan vs. WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green: Green's run has been positioned as a "fluke" reign that is more short-term than anything. That would make a Green win here fun, but it also seems unlikely. Morgan has The Judgement Day to help push her over the top while making Green look like a scrappy underdog who just got overwhelmed by "the numbers game." Morgan benefits more from the win from a character standpoint, so she likely gets it done here. Pick: Liv Morgan wins -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton (Last Man Standing Match): I had hoped that WWE would move on from Rhodes vs. Orton after Sunday Night's Main Event. The company even teased an undisputed WWE title program between Orton and Zayn before going back to the well. It's unlikely that Rhodes loses to his mentor a second time, especially after attempting to give him more edge with the punt. The Last Man Standing stipulation implies finality, so expect Rhodes to carry winning momentum into a new feud. Pick: Cody Rhodes wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)World Tag Team Championship -- The Vision (Bron Breakker & Austin Theory) (c) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans: Breakker and Theory won the belts on July 6 and have not defended the belts a single time on television or at a premium live event. That's a terrible but true fact that shows how little regard the current WWE climate has for tag team wrestling. While Penta has the Money in the Bank briefcase, it seems we're a little ways away from him cashing in his contract, with Roman Reigns dealing with Sami Zayn as well as 946. It can't hurt to give him a tag title run as a way to keep him busy and continue building momentum. If you're not going to use the tag belts as an actual meaningful championship, you can at least use them as a hood ornament for a wrestler you're pushing as a potential future world champion. Pick: Penta & Je'Von Evans win the titles -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)

title: Steve Cherundolo names first U.S. U-23 roster on road to 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games - CBS Sports
description: Matches against Scotland and Ukraine feature six players with senior USMNT call-ups, led by 2024 Olympian Benjami
body:
Matches against Scotland and Ukraine feature six players with senior USMNT call-ups, led by 2024 Olympian Benjamin Cremaschi and eight European-based prospects
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The road to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is underway as Steve Cherundolo's roster for games against Scotland and Ukraine has been named, and it's an experienced group of players. Six players on this roster have been called up to the United States men's national team, and four earned caps during the recent September/October international break, while Parma's Benjamin Cremaschi was a member of the 2024 Olympic squad and is eligible to still be involved in the 2028 edition of the tournament.Looking at the experience with eight players being based abroad and so many being on the fringes of the senior side, it shows just how deep the talent available to Cherundolo is for the Olympics during what is an exciting time for U.S. Soccer. "We're very excited to bring this talented and polished group of players together and begin our journey toward the 2028 Olympic Games," Cherundolo said. "We're eager to get to work, establish our identity and build a strong foundation for what lies ahead. Our first international matches will be a great opportunity to challenge ourselves, compete, and grow together as a team."They'll begin training for this camp alongside the senior team at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, similarly to how the United States women's national team set up their last camp. Not only does it showcase a synergy between the two sides, but it also provides both Cherundolo and Mauricio Pochettino with opportunities to oversee each squad, because when they're called next, considering how young the senior team is, too, there could be shifts between the two squads.It's an important camp as it's Cherundolo's first since taking over the U-23s, so we'll get our first look at how the United States youth stacks up under him against solid opponents from around the world. Given the experience that's available to him and how tight competition will be for the Olympics, as three overage players can go in the 23-man squad for the competition, everyone will need to be on their game immediately.
RosterGoalkeepers (3): Julian Eyestone (Rotherham United/ENG; Dallas, Texas), Duran Ferree (San Diego FC; San Diego, Calif.), Andrew Rick (Philadelphia Union; Berwyn, Pa.)Defenders (8): Luca Bombino (Stoke City/ENG; Saugus, Calif.), Robert Deziel Jr. (Legia Warszawa/POL; West Palm Beach, Fla.), Tate Johnson (Vancouver Whitecaps FC; Tampa, Fla.), Ethan Kohler (New England Revolution; Campbell, Calif.), Drew Murray (WSG Tirol/AUT; San Jose, Calif.), Nolan Norris (FC Dallas; Fort Worth, Texas), Frankie Westfield (Philadelphia Union; Philadelphia, Pa.), Joshua Wynder (New England Revolution; Louisville, Ky.)Midfielders (6): Snyder Brunell (Seattle Sounders FC; Kirkland, Wash.), Matthew Corcoran (Nashville SC; Dallas, Texas), Benjamin Cremaschi (Parma Calcio 1913/ITA; Key Biscayne, Fla.), Taha Habroune (Columbus Crew; Columbus, Ohio), Brooklyn Raines (New England Revolution; Chicago, Ill.), Niko Tsakiris (San Jose Earthquakes; Saratoga, Calif.)
Forwards (6): Cole Campbell (SV 07 Elversberg/GER; Peachtree City, Ga.), Damion Downs (St. Louis City SC; Schwebenried, Germany), Sebastian Gomez (Seattle Sounders FC; Seattle, Wash.), Andre Gitau (1FSV Mainz 05/GER; Richmond, Texas), Marvin Dills (Eintracht Frankfurt/GER; Frankfurt, Germany.), David Vazquez (San Diego FC; Los Angeles, Calif.)

title: NFL in Spain: Bengals star Joe Burrow goes full tourist in Madrid, reveals the one thing he hates the most - CBS Sports
description: The Bengals are fully enjoying their time in the Spanish capital, which has been taken over by Cincinnati fans
body:
The Bengals are fully enjoying their time in the Spanish capital, which has been taken over by Cincinnati fans
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MADRID — With the Bengals playing in Spain this week, the team decided to fly out early to make the most of their trip to Madrid, and it's safe to say that no one was happier about that than Joe Burrow. The Bengals quarterback has gone into full tourist mode since arriving in the Spanish capital on Wednesday morning. Bengals coach Zac Taylor decided to give his guys the day off on Wednesday and a lot of them decided to spend the day exploring the city. For Burrow, that meant a trip to one of Madrid's most iconic museums. "I went to Museo Del Prado on Wednesday," Burrow said during his press conference Friday. "That was cool."Those aren't exactly the words you'd expect to hear out of the mouth of an NFL quarterback just five days before a game, but that's just Burrow being Burrow. Not only is he one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, but he has one of the most unique personalities. 
Burrow, who basically requested to play in Spain back in 2025 after the NFL announced that Madrid would host an NFL game, has been quietly getting pumped about this trip since the day the schedule was released in May. "I was really excited about it; I hadn't been here yet, so that was exciting for me," Burrow said.The Bengals will be the "visiting" team on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET against the Falcons. 
Taylor has done his best to give the team some free time in Madrid, and they'll have even more time to explore the city on Friday evening. Burrow hasn't yet decided what he's going to get into, but he's currently mulling over several options. 
"I'd like to go and see some more museums, and go to an art gallery and do a little shopping, but we'll see," Burrow said. One reason Burrow has enjoyed his time in Spain is that, for the most part, he can walk around without being recognized.
"I love being out here so I can feel like a normal person for a little bit," Burrow said. Of course, that doesn't mean that NO ONE has recognized him. The Bengals star QB said he ran into a group of students that knew exactly who he was. "As far as my recognizability abroad, sometimes, sometimes not," Burrow said. "That's how it goes. I ran into some students studying abroad from the United States the other day when I was walking around, so that was certainly surprising. It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country. I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me."
Burrow didn't pack any special disguises, and that's mostly because he's not in charge of packing his own suitcase, which is probably for the best. Packing a suitcase is apparently the one thing Burrow hates more than anything. For the trip to Madrid, he let his mom and his assistant, Kyle Smith, handle all the packing. "Thank God I don't have to pack anymore," Burrow said. "That's my least favorite thing to do in the entire world, is pack a suitcase for a trip. My mom helped me, Kyle helped me, and we have a good fit for Sunday for sure."Burrow isn't the only Bengals player who has been enjoying his downtime this week. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims visited the Real Casa de Correos, where he made some new friends. 
The fact that Mims was even awake was a good thing for the Bengals, because earlier in the week he was still having trouble adjusting to the six-hour time difference between Madrid and Cincinnati. "So I went to sleep [Wednesday] night. Woke up at 12:30 a.m. CET, watch the whole 76ers game, went back to bed at 3:30 a.m. CET and I woke up at 7:30," Mims told Bengals radio voice Dan Hoard.Based on Cincinnati time, that means Mims went to bed Wednesday afternoon, woke up at 6:30 p.m. ET, watched an NBA game until 9:30 p.m. ET and then woke up for good at 1:30 a.m. ET. Waking up at that hour isn't normal, which is why it makes sense to leave early for an international game, so your players have a chance to get acclimated. 
Mims has been a busy guy this week: Not only did he meet a few police officers, but he also spent some time walking around Madrid with the Bengals offensive line, and at some point on Wednesday, they ran into a Bengals fan.
It's not that surprising to see the offensive line run into a fan, as Bengals fans have taken over Madrid. 
Heading into the weekend, Bengals fans were far outnumbering Falcons fans in Madrid, so Atlanta's home game might not feel like much of a home game. 
First-time overseasFor most Bengals players, this will be their first international game, but Tee Higgins might have them all topped. Not only will this be the first time he's played a game outside the United States, but this trip marked the first time he had ever been to Europe. "Once I landed out here, I was like, 'I can't believe I actually crossed the Atlantic,'" Higgins said Thursday. "It's my first time ever crossing the Atlantic [to] Europe. It's just amazing to me, just knowing where I came from, bringing my family out here, because it's their first time as well, so it's pretty dope. It's surreal. We're definitely going to enjoy our time here, even though it's short."Higgins has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this year. Heading into Week 9, he's one of just two players — along with Jaxon Smith-Njigba — averaging more than 100 receiving yards per game. Higgins has 43 catches for 726 yards, which leads the Bengals (We actually took a close look at why Higgins has been so successful this year, and you can check out the story here). 
Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase have been quite the tandem, and although Chase's numbers haven't been as impressive, he's not complaining, because he loves to see Higgins thrive. "I think it's fun working with Tee and him working with me," Chase said Friday. "We're always making each other better."Speaking of Chase, during the team's off day on Wednesday, he might have been the only one who didn't have fun, at least to start things off. All he wanted was some food, and he couldn't find anything he liked.  
"My first day, I was a little annoyed trying to find some food, and I was saying I miss my chef, but now, I think I'm pretty good," Chase said. "Pretty good" would also be an accurate way to sum up the Bengals right now. At 5-2, the team is surging at the right time, and a win over the Falcons would set up an AFC North showdown, with first place on the line, against the Steelers in Week 10. However, no one on the Bengals' roster is looking ahead to that game just yet. This team is enjoying their time away from home. "This is somewhere I've always wanted to go, and so, to be able to do it while doing what I love, playing football, is really a dream come true for me," Burrow said. Burrow and the Bengals can put the finishing touches on this dream trip by beating the Falcons on Sunday.

schema.headline: NFL in Spain: Bengals star Joe Burrow goes full tourist in Madrid, reveals the one thing he hates the most - CBS Sports

title: Browns name starting QB for Week 9 game vs. Saints: Shedeur Sanders gets nod over Deshaun Watson - CBS Sports
description: Sanders briefly replaced Watson during last Sunday's loss in Pittsburgh
body:
Sanders briefly replaced Watson during last Sunday's loss in Pittsburgh
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Cleveland Browns are making a notable lineup change ahead of Sunday's road game against the New Orleans Saints. Browns coach Todd Monken announced on Friday that quarterback Shedeur Sanders will get his first start of the 2026 season. Sanders will start over Deshaun Watson, who has been labeled as questionable for Sunday's game after he placed in the concussion protocol following last Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson, who returned to practice on Friday and was a limited participant, was sacked eight times during last week's 27-6 loss. He left the game early in the first quarter after taking a big hit from Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker. Sanders briefly entered the game and completed both of his two attempts for two yards. Watson played the majority of last Sunday's game. He threw for a season-high 324 yards on 27 of 39 passing but wasn't able to lead the Browns' offense into the end zone. 
Watson, 31, beat out Sanders for the starting job this summer. While his play has been shaky at times, Watson has played well enough to help Cleveland get off to a surprising 5-3 start. The Browns are currently third in the AFC North standings behind Pittsburgh (6-2) and Cincinnati (5-2). Sanders, a 2025 fifth-round pick, attempted just three passes during Cleveland's first eight games. Last season, he was selected as an alternative for the Pro Bowl while making seven regular-season starts. He went 3-4 as a starter while completing 56.6% of his passes with 7 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. 
On Sunday, the Browns' offense will face a Saints defense that ranked 29th in the NFL in points allowed, 24th in rushing yards allowed and 29th in passing yards allowed. The unit is also a woeful 30th in the NFL in third-down efficiency.

        Serie A is back around Italy for the last weekend of action before the November international break. Inter will host Como on Sunday after a disappointing defeat in the Derby della Madonnina but will meet a team in great form. Elsewhere, Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri faces a match against Lazio that will likely decide his future at the club, while Fiorentina and Juventus meet on Sunday in Florence. Let's take a closer look at what to watch for on Matchday 11: the game, the team and the story you need to know.Game to watch: Inter vs. ComoThe side coached by Cristian Chivu will host Como at San Siro on Sunday, a crucial test for the Nerazzurri after a challenging week. Inter lost the Derby della Madonnina 3-1 to AC Milan last weekend, showing some defensive issues they also faced earlier this season. They responded with a 3-0 win at Feyenoord in the Champions League. Como, meanwhile, thrashed Lens 9-1 on Wednesday in one of the most remarkable performances by an Italian side in the competition's recent history. Inter must now prove to their rivals that they remain the team to beat. However, they face a tough challenge against one of Europe's strongest sides, with Como currently sitting fourth in the league-phase standings, behind only Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG.Team to watch: FrosinoneLooking at the Serie A standings, Frosinone are undoubtedly the team that stands out the most. Coach Massimiliano Alvini, one of the most underrated in the league, deserves the credit for the job done, as Frosinone are currently sixth, with six wins, two draws and only two defeats in the opening 10 games. For comparison, Frosinone have six points more than Napoli, who are eighth with 14 points so far.Story of the week: Allegri's last callSpeaking of Napoli, the Azzurri find themselves in a difficult situation, having collected just 14 points from their opening 10 Serie A matches and already suffered four defeats, including last weekend's away loss to Juventus in Turin. Allegri is now under increasing pressure following the disappointing start to the season, compounded by a heavy 4-1 defeat away to Porto in midweek. For Allegri, the game against Lazio might be his last chance to keep his job before the international break, when changes are not unusual.

title: Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd announce breakup, reveal split happened 'over a year' ago - CBS Sports
description: Bueckers and Fudd began a relationship as college teammates before going No. 1 overall to the Wings in consecutiv
body:
Bueckers and Fudd began a relationship as college teammates before going No. 1 overall to the Wings in consecutive WNBA drafts
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd announced Friday during an episode of Fudd's podcast, "Fudd Around and Find Out," that they are no longer a couple, and haven't been for quite some time. "Alright, well before we continue with anything else, Paige and I have something that we want to share with everyone... We are no longer together," Fudd said. "I don't know how else to say that." Bueckers said the two have not been together for "over a year," a timeframe that spans the entire WNBA season. "I mean, yeah, we're not together anymore. It's been, for everybody wondering, even though we don't have to share, it's been a while," Bueckers said. "It's been like, over a year. And to share that because everybody's gonna be like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this gonna work?' We were not together before she got drafted, so all of those narratives can go to bed.
"She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it, because she's an amazing human, amazing basketball player," Bueckers continued. "And we're still friends, we're still cool and we broke up over a year ago, so we played an entire season together. We're the utmost professionals. We care about basketball and we're still friends. We're still cool."
Bueckers and Fudd first met at a Team USA tryout in 2017. Bueckers committed to play college basketball at UConn and recruited Fudd to join her. They began a romantic relationship at some point when they were teammates at UConn. It became public in July 2025 after they led the Huskies to the NCAA national championship and Bueckers was selected No. 1 overall by the Wings in the WNBA Draft. A year later, the Wings selected Fudd with the No. 1 pick of the 2026 WNBA Draft. At Fudd's introductory press conference in April, the Wings shut down questions regarding the pair's relationship. "I understand why you have to ask that question, but we're gonna respectfully decline on commenting on our players' personal lives," a Wings PR staffer said. 
"Me and Azzi's personal relationship is nobody's business but our own," Bueckers said at the Wings' media day a few weeks later. "What we choose to share is completely up to us." She added that she would not address the topic again during the season.  
        
            
                What's next for Wings? After Paige Bueckers' playoff debut, Dallas must shore up supporting cast
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Fudd's rookie campaign was cut short after 30 games when she underwent season-ending knee surgery. Despite her absence, Bueckers led the Wings to the No. 7 seed and their first playoff appearance since 2023. In the first round, the Wings were up by 16 in a winner-take-all Game 3 against the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries, but collapsed and lost by four. Fudd, who before her injury became the first rookie to win the 3-Point Contest, averaged 13.1 points and 1.7 steals, and shot 39.7% from 3-point range, which was good enough for a spot on the All-Rookie Team. Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists on 51.2/41/87.1 shooting splits, and was one of four players to finish in the top 10 in scoring and assists. She was named to the All-WNBA Second Team for the second time in as many seasons and finished sixth in MVP voting.

title: Waldo Cortes Acosta believes Johnny Walker is learning to run 'for his life' from Alexander Volkov - CBS Sports
description: Cortes Acosta questions Walker's heavyweight potential ahead of their UFC Fight Night main event this weekend
body:
Cortes Acosta questions Walker's heavyweight potential ahead of their UFC Fight Night main event this weekend
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:01 pm ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS -- Waldo Cortes Acosta thinks Johnny Walker is getting ahead of himself. Walker made a successful UFC heavyweight debut last month, but Cortes Acosta says the Brazilian knockout artist will get a reality check against a legitimate heavyweight contender.Cortes Acosta and Walker headline UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Las Vegas. It's a short-notice opportunity for both men, though the stakes differ considerably. Cortes Acosta, the UFC's sixth-ranked heavyweight, risks his standing against an unranked opponent. Meanwhile, Walker can accelerate his climb up the division, but risks moving too fast. The Dominican former professional baseball player isn't intimidated by Walker, especially after hearing what his opponent said about training with Alexander Volkov, who beat Cortes Acosta earlier this year."I heard he told somebody, 'Oh, I know I can knock out Waldo Cortes right now because I train with Alexander Volkov.' But my question is, 'Did Alexander Volkov knock me out?' No. What is he learning from Alexander Volkov? Kicking and running away for his life," Cortes Acosta told CBS Sports. "If this is what you're learning, I'll chase you anywhere. I prepare for people like you or him. I'm well prepared, and I'll go for your head."Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Cortes Acosta doesn't believe Walker's future is at heavyweight. Walker recently defeated Mick Parkin in his divisional debut, but Cortes Acosta dismissed the victory as a fortunate introduction to the weight class. He thinks Walker would be better served returning to light heavyweight."I think he'll have more success at light heavyweight than as a heavyweight," Cortes-Acosta said. "He got lucky to get a chance to fight Parkin first. Every other heavyweight would knock him out in the first round... Now you have a real heavyweight."Winning spectacularly is paramount as the heavyweight division takes center stage to close the year. Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit fight for the UFC heavyweight title next week at UFC 334. Whoever leaves Madison Square Garden with the title will likely face the winner of Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira, set for UFC 335 one month later.
Hokit forced himself into the MMA collective consciousness with crude remarks and bizarre media appearances. His quick success inside the Octagon rewarded him with a UFC heavyweight title shot. Before he blew past Cortes Acosta in the title picture, Hokit had angled to fight the Dominican standout.Cortes Acosta has confronted Hokit on two separate occasions: first for calling him out, and second for mentioning Cortes Acosta's family. According to the Dominican fighter, an intimidated Hokit initially apologized."I think I scared him that time because I finished a fight. I was ready to continue fighting," Cortes Acosta said. "He saw me and said, 'I'm sorry, man. I think you and I can make good money in the future.' 
"If he had been talking shit about my kids at that time, and I found him in the elevator, it would be a whole other problem..."
The second encounter was far less amicable. Hokit doubled down on Cortes Acosta after allegedly apologizing to him behind the scenes. This time, Hokit also referenced Cortes Acosta's nine children. The next time they crossed paths, Hokit had to worry less about Cortes Acosta and more about his wife."My wife wanted to fight with him," Cortes Acosta said. "She's one person who won't tolerate nothing from a woman or a man either."
A lot of things need to shake out in the heavyweight division before Hokit and Cortes Acosta cross paths. The No. 6-ranked heavyweight will take a step in the right direction if he beats Walker on nine days' notice. Flying to Las Vegas for an unranked opponent is a risky gamble. But for Cortes Acosta, who fights for the ninth time in less than two years, such daring is exactly why the UFC called on him to headline Saturday's card."I say yes to any fighter who wants to fight me, or any fighter the UFC puts in there. I never say no," Cortes Acosta said. "I risk everything every time I fight. It's normal for me. I've risked a lot of things in my life, but this is one of the things that has put me in the position I'm in now."*Author's note: Quotes tweaked for clarity.

title: Anxiety Rankings: Notre Dame, BYU suddenly have no room for error after CFP committee reveals rankings - CBS Sports
description: There are very few things in life that can stir emotions within you like college football. For four months a year, millions of Americans
body:
There are very few things in life that can stir emotions within you like college football. For four months a year, millions of Americans decide to put their mental well-being in the hands of a collection of 18- to 24-year-old men they do not know personally. All they know is that they've chosen to wear their preferred uniform. Sometimes this decision brings joy. Other times it brings pain.But what it always brings as kickoff draws near every week is anxiety. There's always the nervous energy of the unknown heading into a game. You can never be sure how things will go, and where the rollercoaster will take you. However, while we all feel it, some of us feel it more than others, and each week, The Anxiety Rankings aim to find the five most anxious places in the country.Welcome to Week 10. Try to stay calm. You'll fail, but try all the same.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. No wiggle room for Notre Dame You know there were already nerves around South Bend, Indiana, on Tuesday before the first College Football Playoff rankings were released because, no matter how confident you might be in your own team, or what you think of it, you know that when you aren't in a conference, your fate is primarily tied to 12 people in a room.After leaving their hats at the door, those 12 sent a pretty strong message to Notre Dame: I wouldn't lose another game if I were you.
The Irish came in at No. 11, which is basically the last spot in the field when you account for the G6 spot. It was clear that, despite being 7-1 on the season, a resume that includes a loss to the best team you've played, and a marquee win of Wisconsin or North Carolina (depending on your preferred power rating) doesn't get anybody on the committee all that excited.The good news for the Irish is you have a chance to prove yourself this weekend. The bad news is if you fail this test, you may not be given another chance. Nobody who cares about Notre Dame football needs to be reminded of this fact. They lived it last season when they lost to Miami and Texas A&M to open the season and then won out against a schedule full of teams that didn't move the needle. If the Irish lose to Miami again this week, this time at home, I'm not so sure wins against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse will save them. The fact of the matter is they'll need help elsewhere. Which, considering how things have gone across college football this season, is well within the realm of possibility.
But you don't want to leave it up to others. When you have a chance to control your fate, it's best to take it, and this week's game is the chance. You're at home. It's supposed to be 37 degrees at kickoff. Miami is without its best player and Heisman hopeful Malachi Toney. If you can't win in this situation, it will be hard to make an argument that you genuinely deserve a spot on the field.Of course, there's the other side of this too. If you win, how much will it be worth to the committee? There's no way to know what kind of logical pretzels those people will twist their minds into. What if they say that beating Miami without Malachi Toney isn't all that impressive? I mean, these are the same people who said they ranked Ohio State No. 12 because the defense gave up a few big plays against USC, while the team two spots ahead of the Buckeyes in the poll (Ole Miss) ranks 104th nationally in explosive play rate allowed (Ohio State ranks 37th). Maybe the fact that Notre Dame ranks first will help?
        
            
                College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 10, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Or maybe they just say things? Who knows!? All Notre Dame knows it is better to win Saturday night.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Holy War has high stakes for BYUWhat a cruel twist of fate that BYU, the team that picked up one of the best wins of the season by beating Notre Dame last month, would be right behind them in this week's Anxiety Rankings despite that win. That's what happens when you follow up a win over the Irish by losing to UCF the very next weekend. The same UCF that followed it up with a sad 41-9 loss at home to Baylor a week later to fall to 4-4.We all know how much the committee loves those wins against teams above .500!Much like Notre Dame's ranking, the committee putting BYU at No. 9 sent a message too. The Notre Dame win doesn't carry nearly enough weight to overcome what looks like a bad loss, so you may want to win against No. 3 Utah this weekend.Now, obviously, BYU would want to beat Utah no matter where anybody was ranked, what was at stake, or if the game was played in a parking lot. They don't call it The Holy War because these two are fond of one another. Still, the game did take on a bit more significance with the rankings because now the Cougars are in a very similar position to the one Notre Dame is in.
If you lose here, you can't be sure winning out against Baylor, Kansas and Cincinnati will get you back into the field. And while BYU would still be alive for a Big 12 title, they would need Texas Tech to lose at least one more game to have a chance to get to the conference title game. It wasn't long ago that it felt like there was a real chance the Big 12 would get at least two teams in the field, and possibly even three. But that was before BYU's loss to UCF and Texas Tech's loss to Cincinnati. Now, when you look around the rankings, while the committee loves them some Utah, they don't seem nearly as impressed by the Big 12 as a whole. Not when they have the Red Raiders ranked behind six Big Ten and SEC teams with two losses, and the Cougars behind two. Also, while Arizona is at No. 22 this week, which helps both BYU and Tech, everybody knows that if the Wildcats suffer another loss (and they do play Utah), they'll be tossed aside very quickly.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Tough stretch looms for TexasThe anxiety in Austin isn't about a lack of respect from the committee. Those 12 hatless gents clearly respect the Longhorns. That's why they put them at No. 7 despite their two losses. Wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss will do that for you, even if one of your losses was to a 4-4 Oklahoma. That resume is why most people were confident that, even if the Longhorns finish the regular season 9-3, they would have a strong chance of making the field.
The problem for Texas is they have to finish at least 9-3. Obviously, this week's game on the road against No. 18 Missouri is a tricky spot. Texas has only played one true road game this season, and it lost to Tennessee 20-17. It's only favored by 2.5 points this week at Missouri, which means that, for all intents and purposes, the outcome of this game is a coin flip.Considering Missouri is ranked, this loss wouldn't kill Texas' hopes. They would just have to win out to have a realistic chance. The problem is, can they win out? Have you seen who the Longhorns play next week? Yeah, they're at LSU.Logically, if Texas lost on the road to Tennessee, and then lost on the road to Missouri, how confident would anyone be in their ability to then go on the road and beat LSU? Likely at night (Lane Kiffin has already started campaigning for it).
It's not a must-win for Texas this weekend, but it's definitely a better-not-lose. There are plenty of nerves in Austin heading into Saturday.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Ole Miss faces must-win game vs. GeorgiaDoes the committee respect the SEC? Clearly. There would be five SEC teams in the field based on this week's ranking, and three of them have two losses. Meanwhile, one-loss teams from the Big 12 and ACC are on the outside looking in. But while Ole Miss is one of those three two-loss SEC teams, they aren't at the top of the pecking order.Alabama is at No. 5, Texas at No. 7, and then there's Ole Miss at No. 10. That's a very clear message from the committee: you can't afford a third loss. Those others can, but not you. When Ole Miss looks over its shoulder, it not only sees Notre Dame right behind it, but a group of other two-loss teams in Ohio State, Tennessee and LSU. 
So, hey, good luck against No. 2 Georgia this week! That shouldn't be too difficult a game to win, right? Making matters worse for Ole Miss is that, even if they weren't playing this weekend, their resume is likely to get weaker. One of their two losses was to Texas, while their second-best win was against Missouri. With those two playing one another, either the Texas or Missouri win will look "worse" on their resume. And while Florida counts as a ranked win for now, can you really trust Florida not to drop another game at this point? And what if LSU loses to Alabama? Then your strongest win gets weaker too.So, essentially, this Georgia game is a must-win. If you get it, you're in great shape. If you don't, and your resume weakens elsewhere, remaining games against Oklahoma, Wofford and a Kamario-less Mississippi State will do nothing for you. Especially when there are so many teams lined up right behind you, ready to step on your head if you fall.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Pressure mounts on Michigan's Kyle WhittinghamWhile the College Football Playoff is the source of the most anxiety this weekend, it's not the only reason people are nervous. No, Kyle Whittingham probably isn't even thinking about the playoff these days. He's more likely thinking "I wonder if I'm going to get a second year at Michigan. I wonder if I even want one."
It's been a bad season to be a Wolverine. You're 5-3 overall and 2-3 in Big Ten play. You aren't ranked anywhere, let alone in the playoff conversation. And even your wins have been rage-inducing. You beat Penn State at home by 3 in an ugly game, and last week you beat Rutgers 28-21. Sure, the game wasn't as close as the score suggested, but it was still too close. Let's not forget Michigan has beaten Rutgers by scores of 78-0 and 52-0 in the last decade.If there's a silver lining to last week, it's that Tommy Carr had his best game yet. Perhaps he'll continue to improve, and this Michigan team will provide reasons to be optimistic about next year down the home stretch. Or maybe they'll lose at home this weekend to Little Brother.Michigan State is a mess this season. They're 2-6 on the year and 0-5 in Pat Fitzgerald's first season. The injury report is more of an injury novel. But you know what would make this painful season feel great in East Lansing? A win over Michigan. Man, it would feel great to twist that knife and really turn 2026 into an abject disaster for the state rival, and Pat Fitzgerald loves to save his best for his team's biggest games.
And if you're Kyle Whittingham, you can't let Fitzy get you. You cannot afford a loss to Michigan State, especially when your final three games of the season are at Oregon, vs. UCLA and at Ohio State. A loss this weekend suddenly puts your ability to even reach a bowl game in jeopardy.A loss this weekend means there's a new coach at Michigan next season.

title: MLB betting scandal: Bo Naylor testifies in defense of Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz - CBS Sports
description: Naylor was behind the plate when many of the pitches, alleged to be rigged to benefit b
body:
Naylor was behind the plate when many of the pitches, alleged to be rigged to benefit bettors, were thrown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Former Cleveland Guardians catcher Bo Naylor on Thursday testified in federal court that he perceived nothing untoward about disputed pitches thrown by former All-Star closer Emmanuel Clase and his former Guardians teammate Luis Ortiz, ESPN reports. Naylor, who played five seasons for the Guardians, appeared as a witness for the defense in the ongoing federal trial in which prosecutors allege that Clase and Ortiz rigged multiple pitches for the benefit of co-conspiring bettors. In Clase's case, he's alleged to have done so in 17 games across a two-year period beginning in May 2023. Naylor, now a member of the Milwaukee Brewers, was catcher for some of Clase's disputed appearances during that span, including seven of the 18 pitches he's alleged to have rigged. ESPN's David Purdum writes:  Naylor, a defense witness, was shown video replays of some of the pitches the government alleges were predetermined by Clase or Ortiz as part of the scheme. Naylor was behind the plate for many of them and said they looked like common sliders outside the strike zone. He said the scouting reports on the hitters Ortiz faced during the two pitches in question indicated that sliders low and away would be a "weapon."In November 2025, Clase and Ortiz were indicted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. According to the Department of Justice, both pitchers "agreed in advance with their co-conspirators to throw specific types of pitches and speeds of pitches." The Department of Justice alleged that the pair made at least $450,000 by rigging outings and throwing specific pitches to benefit bettors who wagered on the outcomes of those pitches.Both Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to those charges in November of last year. Clase and Ortiz have been on administrative leave since late June 2025 while Major League Baseball investigates. MLB has the authority to discipline the pitchers regardless of how the criminal trial plays out. 
The pair could face up to 65 years in prison if convicted on the charges of wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery, and money laundering conspiracy.

title: Myles Garrett on track to be activated ahead of Rams Week 9 matchup vs. Commanders - CBS Sports
description: Los Angeles could be getting its star pass rusher back
body:
Los Angeles could be getting its star pass rusher back
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Rams were dubbed a superteam coming into the 2026 season but have largely fallen short of that declaration as they enter Week 9 with a 4-4 record. That said, part of the reason for the underwhelming start is the club not having its biggest offseason acquisition, Myles Garrett, in the fold. That may be about to change. The star pass rusher and defending Defensive Player of the Year is on track to be activated off of injured reserve ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Washington Commanders, head coach Sean McVay confirmed Friday. Garrett, who has been battling a knee injury, has been limited in practice this week and all indications point toward him playing this weekend.  Garrett had been hampered by a knee injury dating all the way back to training camp. Despite missing the bulk of camp, the 30-year-old suited up in Los Angeles' season-opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. However, Garrett was largely ineffective in his Rams debut, recording just his fourth career game in which he totaled zero tackles. The injury clearly hobbled him as he played just 39 snaps. After the contest, Garrett acknowledged that he was not 100%, saying, "I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be, and I've shown that I've been before."
That then led Garrett to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his knee, which found him landing on injured reserve. He has since missed Los Angeles' last seven games. This extended absence is a rarity for Garrett, as he's typically been a durable piece to his prior defenses. Over the last five seasons (2021-2025), he missed just two of his 85 games played. Entering Week 9, the Rams rank 17th in the NFL in pressure rate (36.3%) and 27th in sack rate (4.4%), so the addition of Garrett back into this unit should give the pass rush a much-needed boost. Of course, Garrett was at the center of arguably the biggest blockbuster trade of the offseason. On June 1, LA sent pass rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-rounder, a 2028 second-rounder, and a 2029 third-round pick to the Cleveland Browns in exchange for Garrett. The Rams also reached an agreement on a restructured five-year, $208.2 million deal following the trade. 
Before this deal, Garrett spent the first nine years of his career with the Browns, where he won two Defensive Player of the Year awards, including in 2025 after he set the single-season sack record (23).

description: With Simmons locked in, Missouri can now build a winning roster around him
body:
With Simmons locked in, Missouri can now build a winning roster around him
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Missouri has re-signed quarterback Austin Simmons for the 2027 season, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. That gives the Tigers stability at the most important position on the field ahead of what could be a hectic offseason in the portal.After beginning the 2025 season as the starting quarterback at Ole Miss, Simmons lost his job to Trinidad Chambliss and transferred to Missouri in the offseason. Through eight games, Simmons has been an excellent fit and has the Tigers in the mix to reach the College Football Playoff.In his first season as a Tiger, Simmons has completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,952 yards, 16 touchdowns and two interceptions. It helps that Simmons has some of the best weapons in the SEC around him, as Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode are two of the top eight receivers in the conference.That trio has powered a passing offense that ranks fourth in the conference at 257.1 yards per game and 26th in EPA per dropback at 0.19. That aerial attack has been the biggest driver of Missouri's offense this season, and that should remain the case in 2027.
With Simmons guaranteed to remain in Columbia, that allows Missouri to start getting its ducks in a row for portal season. If the Tigers play their cards correctly, they could be a force next fall.Retaining weapons, replacing OLParticularly when it comes to the offensive side of the ball, Missouri should have the chance to retain most of its production. Getting the quarterback -- presumably the most expensive player -- locked in will help the Tigers get more cost certainty as it looks to re-sign other players.The top priorities will obviously be the wide receivers. Olugbode, who has 584 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, is only a sophomore. He will play at least one more college season, and Missouri needs to make sure he doesn't go anywhere.
Lee, on the other hand, leads the SEC in receiving yards and is a senior. He could chase his NFL dreams, but if he did want to return, there would likely be plenty of interest from other teams. Assuming uses that fifth year of eligibility, Lee might be expensive to re-sign, but it would be worth it based on what he's done with Simmons so far.The running back situation is similar. Jamal Roberts leads the SEC with 1,005 rushing yards and could make the jump to the NFL. Ahmad Hardy could do the same thing, but he may want to prove to NFL scouts that he's fully healed from the gunshot wound he suffered earlier this year. If Missouri could keep at least one of those players, it would be a great sign for the 2027 offense.Where the Tigers may need to do some work in the portal is along the offensive line. Missouri has several fifth-year seniors on the interior, and true senior Cayden Lee could be a 2027 NFL Draft pick at left tackle. If the Tigers lose all of those players, they'll have to go portaling, but at least inking Simmons to a new deal now will help the team develop a game plan for rebuilding the offensive line.
Perhaps most importantly, having a talented quarterback like Simmons makes Missouri an appealing spot for current players and prospective portal additions alike. While other teams are bound for a shake-up behind center, Missouri has a proven commodity at quarterback, and that's something Eli Drinkwitz will be able to pitch.

schema.headline: Austin Simmons re-signs with Missouri: Tigers set for high expectations in 2027 with star QB returning - CBS Sports

title: Kansas City Current and Angel City FC bring high scoring squads to quarterfinal action - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City Current host Angel City in the NWSL quarterfinals
body:
Kansas City Current host Angel City in the NWSL quarterfinals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When two of the NWSL's highest-scoring teams meet in a playoff game, you can expect fireworks. The Kansas City Current will host Angel City FC at CPKC Stadium on Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on CBS,  and the two sides are peaking at the right time as the postseason begins, with both clubs finishing the regular season with 54 goals scored.Kansas City have a 32-game home unbeaten streak that dates back to 2024, making the riverfront home a place where visiting teams typically lose. Angel City return to the playoffs for the first time since 2023 on a 10-game unbeaten run, and are equally relentless on the road. Angel City won the first regular-season meeting between them at BMO Stadium, 2-1, back in May, while the rematch in August ended in a 1-1 draw in Kansas City.Both teams took different paths to reach the playoffs and match up well on paper, but something has to give, and the winner advances to the semifinals.Here's everything you need to know about the big game on CBS:Kansas City playoff returnThe 2025 NWSL Shield winners had a tough start to the season. After the team was bounced out of the 2025 playoffs in the opening round, Vlatko Andonovski moved to an executive role while the club brought in Chris Armas as new head coach. Two-time Golden Boot winner Temwa Chawinga started the 2026 season on the injury report, and the club suffered multiple player departures, including Bia Zaneratto and Claire Hutton.\The early results were rough, with zero wins in the opening four games of the season, and players either not gelling together or occupying similar spaces or even running into each other. They maneuvered the first quarter of the schedule closer to the bottom half of the league table than the playoff line.
There was a doubling down of questions about Armas, his limited knowledge of the NWSL and women's pro soccer, and whether or not injuries or absences kept him from rolling out a complete lineup. But things finally shifted with the spring and, of course, the return of Chawinga.Midfielder Croix Bethune, who was acquired in preseason, grew into her role and set an NWSL single-season record with 11 assists, including six game-winning assists. Forward Haley Hopkins had a breakout season; after being traded to the club in 2025, she co-leads the team with Chawinga in goals (12) this year. The roster's 54 goals are split across 13 different players."I'd say that what's clear is that we've just come together. Is it the right time? It's just an important time of year to have most of your players healthy. We're at a good fitness level. The team has been together all year, but you have to go through things sometimes to, you know, see your best version. And sometimes it's adversity. And when does that come? I've always said that oftentimes teams experience that in a season, and we had a lot of it this year," Armas told CBS Sports.
"On the outside, they might just see we're not getting results, or they might ignore some of the performances for a long time. Things like XG, and like, we just had a process. We talk about sticking to it, but the team has been through a lot of change, a lot of injuries this year early on to key players, and all along I know whether a team believes it or not, we were finding different ways of doing things. Some of it was by design because I'm a new coach to the team. Some of it was finding different ways to score and different people to rely on, and different ways to attack and create chances. And even some of our high press and mid block, and some of it was different ways of doing things," Armas explained.All of the ups and downs and adjustments were ultimately seeds planted along the way, Armas also said. The playoffs are maybe just the time to harvest, but mostly it's about how the team is performing on a consistent basis now, and how that's reverberated throughout the locker room."I think that we've gotten to see some of that come to fruition throughout the season, but consistently right now, which then is the belief and confidence that comes, and that's contagious. It's contagious for Angel City. It's contagious for teams like Gotham and Washington, like some of these teams that have done really well. And it's been contagious for us ... So we're in a good moment, and it all resets because we play against another team in a good moment. But we like where we're at. We like who we are, and we're up for it," he said.
Angel City's remarkable second halfMaybe Angel City's executives cracked the code to a long season. If you're not doing well and there is still a ton of season left, maybe just go ahead and make the call. They made multiple. While big gambles don't always pay off, they are paying off right now for Angel City.First, the club parted ways with head coach Alexander Straus in June. After a three-game win streak to open the season, the club hit a massive speed bump and managed only one win over its next eight games. They then used the summer break to make another bold move, trading $850,000 in intraleague transfer funds to the Kansas City Current for forward Ally Sentnor.With Leif Gunnar Smerud as interim head coach, Sentnor's addition, and the return of Savy King to the backline, the club went on one of its best runs in club history. The group has one loss in its last 14 games and is on a 10-game unbeaten streak heading into the quarterfinals. They co-lead the regular season with Kansas City in goals scored (54), with as many different goal scorers (13) as their playoff opponent.
Sveindis Jonsdottir and Maiara Niehues each set club records for single-season goals, scoring 19 between them. But the defense has been just as essential to the surge in form. Goalkeeper Angelina Anderson posted 10 clean sheets, and fullbacks King and Evelyn Shores elevated their play, with Shores leading the team with eight assists."We are in a good place. We're gonna have to keep doing what we've been doing well, which is play the game and the situation in front of us. We have been able to go to very different games and game scenarios, and opponents and stadiums, and sort of managed to find a way to win, and done it with courage and with the attacking mindset," Smerud told CBS Sports."We scored a lot of goals. I think most in the league, together with Kansas. So it's to go out there and be us, and then of course be prepared for. It's a home playoff game for them, and they will certainly want to win it. But we have to be ready from the start. That's the main thing. And we can for sure go there and win this game. But it's not going to come for free," he said.
What's nextThe NWSL quarterfinals are underway; the winner of Kansas City Current vs. Angel City will face the winner of Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign in the semifinals. The semifinal round of the NWSL playoffs will take place on Nov. 14 and 15.

schema.headline: Kansas City Current and Angel City FC bring high scoring squads to quarterfinal action - CBS Sports

title: Antonio Brown avoids jail time, receives punishment after plea deal in Miami shooting - CBS Sports
description: The former NFL star was accused of opening fire at a man last year
body:
The former NFL star was accused of opening fire at a man last year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Former NFL wide receiver Antonio Brown will not serve jail time after he pleaded guilty Friday to a lesser charge stemming from a shooting incident at a boxing event in Miami last year. The Super Bowl-winning ex-player was originally sought on one charge of attempted murder in May 2025 after a fight allegedly took place between Brown and several other individuals shortly after a celebrity boxing event. Brown pleaded guilty this week to aggravated assault with a firearm and received three years of probation. Brown will undergo a mandatory psychological evaluation and may have to attend weekly counseling if mandated by a judge."My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn't refuse," Brown's defense attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, told reporters. "Probation was too good to turn down, and we're both very excited about the outcome."
Videos from the altercation circulated on social media, as did pictures of Brown in handcuffs. Brown later posted on social media claiming he was jumped by people trying to take his jewelry. "Regarding the boxing event that happened last night," Brown wrote at the time. "I was jumped by multiple individuals who tried to steal my jewelry and cause physical harm to me. Contrary to some video circulating, Police temporarily detained me until they received my side of the story and then released me. I WENT HOME THAT NIGHT AND WAS NOT ARRESTED."I will be talking to my legal council [sic] and attorneys on pressing charges on the individuals that jumped me. I will keep you all posted step-by-step on the process. Thank you for the support and love."
Brown last played in the NFL for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the 2021 season when he stormed off the field shirtless after getting into a heated argument with then-coach Bruce Arians.He said he was returning to the league to play for the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, but nothing materialized. In June 2024, Brown filed for bankruptcy, blaming lawsuits and others for his financial misfortunes.Five years prior to filing, Brown served an eight-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy as a result of sexual and personal misconduct allegations levied against him.
From 2010-18 with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Brown was named to the Pro Bowl seven times and was a four-time All-Pro. He played for the New England Patriots for one game in 2019 before he was cut for sending threatening text messages to a woman. He spent his final two seasons with the Buccaneers.

schema.headline: Antonio Brown avoids jail time, receives punishment after plea deal in Miami shooting - CBS Sports
